factors: The source recommends a multi-agent architecture with file, remote, browser and mobile control surfaces.
The feature and throughput claims have different evidence strength and an operator-cost counterargument.
complexity.rationale: Though only 8:29 long, the source makes consequential coordination and authorization claims, warranting an extended original analysis rather than a feature recap.

sourceMap.rationale: The opening lost-tab problem motivates a multi-agent coordination interface rather than proving an output curve.
The five-attempt worktree example separates concurrent file paths but leaves shared resources and integration unresolved.
The WebGL terminal passage proposes smoother high-output display without a measured comparison.
The CLI passage says an agent can drive worktree, snapshot, click and fill operations in the orchestrator.
The mobile segment introduces pairing and remote steering; telemetry is a distinct first-party policy statement.
The supported-agent list and general CLI compatibility claim describes launcher breadth, not demonstrated feature parity.

sourceCoverage.rationale: Six source moments and chapter anchors cover Orca’s central worktree, interface, CLI and mobile claims, while clearly separating the later original synthesis.

supportingArgument.rationale: Unified worktree and diff visibility plausibly reduces navigation and lost-state cost for teams already running multiple agents, and may improve operator judgment.

evidenceRoles.rationale: The exact video establishes what the speaker argued; a pinned product README and vendor docs describe features, while Git documentation constrains worktree mechanics and no deployment outcome is independently measured.

counterargument.rationale: A single integrated UI may enforce controls more consistently than scattered terminals and scripts; the Reader grants that possibility while requiring an actual permissions and outcome test.

tradeoffs.rationale: Concurrent agents reduce file-path collision but can increase semantic integration, shared-service effects and human review load; remote and mobile modes change data custody.

falsifiability.rationale: A matched three-configuration task suite compares accepted output, reviewer minutes, cost, target errors and recovery after simulated uncertain writes.

originalSynthesis.rationale: The Reader treats the worktree as a file boundary and the fleet interface as a potential control plane whose value depends on accepted results and accountable effects.

performance.rationale: The WebGL terminal and multiple-agent throughput claims are labeled unmeasured; a controlled comparison measures latency and accepted task quality.

economics.rationale: The proposed comparison includes operator time, duplicated attempts, token spend and hosting cost instead of treating agent count as output.

threatGovernance.rationale: The article identifies agent-operated CLI, prompt content, remote hosts, mobile relay and telemetry as distinct authority or data paths without alleging a breach.

decisionRationale: A real independent read-only editorial reviewer accepted the exact current article, mapped source cues, graph and privacy boundary for owner review after one corrected timestamp.
